newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak exports continue to lag behind imports.
newsitem.headline: Slovak exports continue to lag behind imports.

text.p: Import growth continued to outpace the rise in exports in May, pushing the Slovak trade deficit to 29.859 billion crowns for the first five months of the year, the Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said on Wednesday.

SUSR said imports totalled 149.117 billion crowns in the first five months of 1997, a year-on-year rise of 13.8 percent, while exports totalled 119.257 billion crowns, up 13.2 percent over the January-May period of last year.
The fastest rising items on import side were audio and video equipment, which jumped 62.3 percent year-on-year and totalled 13.694 billion crowns.
Fossil fuels and mineral oils accounted for the largest portion of goods brought into the country, totalling 26.409 billion crowns, a 20 percent year-on-year increase.

Technological imports, including equipment for upgrading the ageing Jaslovske Bohunice nuclear power plant and the completion of the Mochovce nuclear plant, totalled 23.862 billion crowns, up 24.7 percent year-on-year.
The fastest rising export articles were cars, aircrafts and ships -- totalling together 16.21 billion crowns -- which increased by 78.6 percent against January-May period 1996.

Main export items included steel and stell products which totalled 26.374 billion crowns and were up 3.3 percent year-on-year. Exports of various machines and unspecified instruments totalled 15.979 billion crowns, up some by 13.7 percent over the same period last year.
The Czech Republic remains Bratislava's main trading partner, accounting for 27.9 percent of s exports and 23.3 percent of its imports.

The Russian Federation accounted for 15.5 percent of Slovak imports, followed by Germany with 15.4 percent and Italy with 5.4 percent. Other main Slovak export partners were Germany, accounting for 23.5 percent, and Austria with 6.5 percent.
Slovakia's trade deficit with OECD countries totalled 9.05 billion crowns in the first five months of 1997, while the trade gap with EU states totalled 4.494 billion crowns.
